+#### Joint reads
+
+With `"joint": true`, a diffusion model reads several questions from one canvas in
+one denoising step: the prompt numbers the questions, and each answer is read at
+its slot in a `number: answer` line. A one-question request is read per
+question, as without `joint`.
+
+Questions that do not fit the served canvas (`--diffusion-config
+'{"canvas_length": N}'`) are split, in order, into the fewest even runs that
+fit. Each run is one engine request and counts once for admission.
+
+The response adds a `joint` object, `null` when each question was read on its own:
+
+```json
+"joint": {"canvases": [{"questions": ["urgent", "bucket", "tone"], "width": 16, "slots": [2, 6, 11]}]}
+```
+
+- Answers can differ from per-question reads, since the slots see each other
+  and the question order.
+- `usage.output_tokens` counts each canvas once, up to its last slot.
+- Joint reads take the same limits as per-question reads: 64 questions per
+  request, no thinking, and each prompt plus its canvas within `max_model_len`.
+- `/v1/decisions` takes the same `joint` field as a vLLM extension.
+

+def _negative_halfway_threshold() -> tuple[float, torch.Tensor]:
+    # Top FP32 key of the coarse bin holding -1.0: an FP16 halfway point that
+    # rounds into the bin while the next keys round into the bin above.
+    def coarse_bin(x: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
+        bits = x.half().view(torch.int16).to(torch.int32) & 0xFFFF
+        key = torch.where(bits >= 0x8000, ~bits & 0xFFFF, bits | 0x8000)
+        return key >> 6
+
+    one = torch.tensor([-1.0])
+    base = int(one.view(torch.int32))
+    bits = base - torch.arange(0, 1 << 14, dtype=torch.int32)
+    values = bits.view(torch.float32)
+    in_bin = coarse_bin(values) == coarse_bin(one)
+    top = int(in_bin.nonzero().max())
+    near = values[top + 1 : top + 2048]
+    assert bool((coarse_bin(near) == coarse_bin(one) + 1).all())
+    return float(values[top]), near
+

+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright contributors to the vLLM project
+from typing import TYPE_CHECKING
+
+import torch
+
+from vllm.distributed import get_ep_group
+
+if TYPE_CHECKING:
+    from vllm.v1.worker.gpu_model_runner import GPUModelRunner
+
+
+class EplbCheckExtension:
+    model_runner: "GPUModelRunner"
+
+    def check_eplb_replica_slots(self) -> str | None:
+        """Redundant expert slots must hold their source expert's weights."""
+        eplb_state = self.model_runner.eplb_state
+        assert eplb_state is not None
+        state = next(iter(eplb_state.model_states.values()))
+        sums = [
+            sum(
+                torch.stack([e.view(torch.uint8).sum(dtype=torch.int64) for e in w])
+                for w in layer_weights
+            )
+            for layer_weights in state.model.expert_weights
+        ]
+        sums = get_ep_group().all_gather(torch.stack(sums), dim=1).tolist()
+        bad = sum(
+            s[slot] != s[p2l.index(logical)]
+            for s, p2l in zip(sums, state.physical_to_logical_map.tolist())
+            for slot, logical in enumerate(p2l)
+        )
+        return f"{bad} redundant expert slots differ from their source" if bad else None

+  ## GB200: InferenceX AgentX aggregated (Dynamo + vLLM)
+
+  The GB200 AgentX lane in [SemiAnalysis InferenceX](https://inferencex.semianalysis.com/) (`minimaxm3-fp4-gb200-dynamo-vllm-agentic-agg-mtp`, [SemiAnalysisAI/InferenceX#4281](https://github.com/SemiAnalysisAI/InferenceX/pull/4281)) serves the NVFP4 checkpoint with the GQA EAGLE3 draft (three speculative tokens) as one aggregated vLLM worker behind the Dynamo frontend's KV-aware router. TP4 runs on one 4-GPU GB200 tray; TP8 spans two trays. Image `vllm/vllm-openai:nightly-5555a2d8f7116b2b4877f66516f4128176cf722a@sha256:8896fd7b29fc4ee7ce839f146cb4757984c476ec79d0234ffa8c995dee6e339a`, Dynamo `1.6.0.dev20261016` (`pip install ai-dynamo==1.6.0.dev20261016`).
+
+  In the command builder, pick **GB200** and the **NVFP4** variant (the builder keeps the current variant when you switch hardware, so select NVFP4 explicitly), turn on **Spec Decoding → GQA** and **Text-only**, and use **Single-node TP** for TP4 or **Multi-node TP** with 2 nodes for TP8. That renders the worker flags and environment below as a `vllm serve` command. Direct links: [TP4](https://recipes.vllm.ai/MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-M3?hardware=gb200&variant=nvfp4&features=tool_calling,reasoning,spec_decoding,text_only&fmode=spec_decoding:eagle3_gqa&strategy=single_node_tp) and [TP8 on two trays](https://recipes.vllm.ai/MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-M3?hardware=gb200&variant=nvfp4&features=tool_calling,reasoning,spec_decoding,text_only&fmode=spec_decoding:eagle3_gqa&strategy=multi_node_tp&nodes=2). The GB200 **Verified** badge applies to this NVFP4 profile only; the GQA draft and TP8 all-reduce overrides also apply to the other variants on GB200, which were not qualified.
+
+  For the host-KV-offload points, don't use the **KV Offload → Simple** pill as is: its budget is fixed at 220 GiB per rank (880 GiB per 4-GPU tray) with `lazy_offload: false`, which is more host memory than a GB200 tray can give KV blocks. Replace its `--kv-transfer-config` with the qualified one below and set `VLLM_USE_SIMPLE_KV_OFFLOAD=1`. The per-concurrency settings in this table, the Dynamo KV-router frontend and its services stay in this guide.
+
+  | Clients | TP | `--max-num-seqs` | Host KV offload | CUDA graph capture sizes |
+  |---:|---:|---:|---|---|
+  | 1 | 4 | 2 | none | `1,2,4,8` |
+  | 1 | 8 | 2 | none | `1,2,4,8` |
+  | 10 | 4 | 16 | none | `1,2,4` then every 4 up to `64` |
+  | 20 | 4 | 8 | SimpleCPUOffload | every 4 from `4` to `32` |
+  | 25 | 4 | 16 | SimpleCPUOffload | every 4 from `4` to `64` |
+  | 30 | 4 | 45 | SimpleCPUOffload | every 4 from `4` to `180` |
+
+  Every list ends with `256,512,1024,2048` and uses `{"cudagraph_mode":"FULL_AND_PIECEWISE","cudagraph_capture_sizes":[...]}`. Sizes 1 and 2 give the drafter's decode steps full CUDA graphs at concurrency 1.
+
+  The InferenceX throughput points replaced block verification with synthetic rejection at the committed golden EAGLE3-GQA acceptance length (2.78 for MiniMax-M3 with three draft tokens, thinking on; [`minimaxm3_eagle3_gqa.yaml`](https://github.com/SemiAnalysisAI/InferenceX/blob/main/golden_al_distribution/minimaxm3_eagle3_gqa.yaml)) so every point is measured at the same acceptance rate. Production serving keeps the default rejection sampler, as in the command below; the lane's accuracy evals ran that way.
+
+  ### Services and environment
+
+  Start etcd and NATS (JetStream on, 32 MB max payload) once:
+
+  ```bash
+  etcd --listen-client-urls http://0.0.0.0:2379 --advertise-client-urls http://<infra-host>:2379
+  printf 'max_payload: 33554432\njetstream {}\n' > nats.conf && nats-server -c nats.conf
+  ```
+
+  On every worker tray (and on the frontend host, point the same two variables at the services):
+
+  ```bash
+  export ETCD_ENDPOINTS=http://<infra-host>:2379 NATS_SERVER=nats://<infra-host>:4222
+  export VLLM_FLOAT32_MATMUL_PRECISION=high VLLM_FLASHINFER_ALLREDUCE_BACKEND=trtllm
+  export NCCL_CUMEM_ENABLE=1 NCCL_MNNVL_ENABLE=1 NCCL_NVLS_ENABLE=1
+  export UCX_MEMTYPE_CACHE=n UCX_TLS=cuda_copy,cuda_ipc,rc
+  ```
+
+  Set `UCX_NET_DEVICES` and `NCCL_IB_HCA` to the node's RDMA devices. For TP8 across two trays, use `VLLM_FLASHINFER_ALLREDUCE_BACKEND=mnnvl` instead of `trtllm`. Loading the 1M-context engine takes a while, so raise `VLLM_ENGINE_READY_TIMEOUT_S` and `VLLM_EXECUTE_MODEL_TIMEOUT_SECONDS` well above their defaults.
+
+  ### Worker
+
+  ```bash
+  python3 -m dynamo.vllm --model nvidia/MiniMax-M3-NVFP4 --served-model-name nvidia/MiniMax-M3-NVFP4 \
+    --request-plane tcp --device-ids 0,1,2,3 \
+    --tensor-parallel-size 4 --pipeline-parallel-size 1 --trust-remote-code \
+    --attention-config '{"backend":"FLASHINFER","use_trtllm_attention":true,"indexer_kv_dtype":"fp8","minimax_m3_msa_decode_backend":"cutlass"}' \
+    --kv-cache-dtype fp8 --block-size 128 --enable-prefix-caching \
+    --speculative-config '{"method":"eagle3","model":"Inferact/MiniMax-M3-EAGLE3-GQA","num_speculative_tokens":3,"attention_backend":"FLASHINFER","use_local_argmax_reduction":true}' \
+    --max-model-len 1048576 --max-num-batched-tokens 16384 --max-num-seqs <S> \
+    --compilation-config '{"cudagraph_mode":"FULL_AND_PIECEWISE","cudagraph_capture_sizes":[<sizes from the table>,256,512,1024,2048]}' \
+    --gpu-memory-utilization 0.9 --no-enable-flashinfer-autotune --stream-interval 20 --language-model-only \
+    --kv-events-config '{"publisher":"zmq","topic":"kv-events","enable_kv_cache_events":true,"endpoint":"tcp://*:5200"}' \
+    --reasoning-parser minimax_m3 --dyn-reasoning-parser minimax_m3 --dyn-tool-call-parser minimax_m3
+  ```
+
+  For TP8, run the same command on both trays with `--tensor-parallel-size 8 --nnodes 2 --node-rank <0|1> --master-addr <first-tray-ip>`, adding `--headless` on node rank 1.
+
+  For the host-KV-offload points, also set `VLLM_USE_SIMPLE_KV_OFFLOAD=1` and add:
+
+  ```bash
+  --kv-transfer-config '{"kv_connector":"SimpleCPUOffloadConnector","kv_role":"kv_both","kv_connector_extra_config":{"cpu_bytes_to_use":777389080576,"cpu_bytes_to_use_per_rank":194347270144,"lazy_offload":true}}'
+  ```
+
+  That gives each of the four ranks about 181 GiB of pinned host memory for KV blocks.
+
+  ### Frontend
+
+  ```bash
+  export ETCD_ENDPOINTS=http://<infra-host>:2379 NATS_SERVER=nats://<infra-host>:4222 DYN_REQUEST_PLANE=tcp
+  export DYN_TOKENIZER=fastokens DYN_TOKENIZER_CACHE_BYTES=8589934592 DYN_TCP_REQUEST_TIMEOUT=60
+  python3 -m dynamo.frontend --trust-remote-code \
+    --router-mode kv --router-kv-events --router-temperature 0 \
+    --router-session-affinity-ttl-secs 14400 --kv-cache-block-size 128
+  ```
+
+  The KV router uses the workers' KV events to send each request to the worker holding its prefix, and session affinity keeps a conversation on that worker: send a stable conversation ID in the `X-Dynamo-Session-ID` request header. This Dynamo build warns that `--router-temperature` is deprecated and will be removed in v1.7; newer builds take `router_temperature` in the default policy parameters of `--router-policy-config`.
+
   ## Quantized Variant (MXFP4 on MI355X)
 
   [`amd/MiniMax-M3-MXFP4`](https://huggingface.co/amd/MiniMax-M3-MXFP4)

+      # B200 DEP2 at c24/c32 (SemiAnalysisAI/InferenceX#3837): FlashInfer sparse MLA,

@@ -888,23 +909,69 @@ guide: |
   configuration (`--max-cudagraph-capture-size 8190`),
   `--max-num-batched-tokens 8192` and `--max-num-seqs 256`; B200, GB200 and
   GB300 add Engram CPU offload and otherwise inherit the shared Blackwell
-  settings. Scheduler limits are workload-dependent at TP2, so size
+  settings. B200 is the exception for both strategies: it renders the qualified B200
+  AgentX settings described in **AgentX tuning on NVIDIA GPUs**, so B200 DEP uses
+  `FLASHINFER_MLA_SPARSE_DSV41`, `{"enable_flashinfer_autotune":true,"moe_backend":"deep_gemm_mega_moe"}`,
+  `{"cpu_offload":true,"embedding_across_dp":true}` and `--max-num-seqs 32`.
+  Scheduler limits are workload-dependent at TP2, so size
   `--max-num-batched-tokens` and `--max-cudagraph-capture-size` for your own
   serving profile. For high interactivity on any of them, use
   `--tensor-parallel-size 4`.
 
   ## AgentX tuning on NVIDIA GPUs
 
-  On B200, TP2 at concurrency 1 uses `--engram-config '{"cpu_offload":true,"use_thp":true}'`,
-  `--max-num-seqs 8` and `--max-num-batched-tokens 4096`. DEP2 (TP1 x DP2 with expert
-  parallelism) serves concurrency 8 to 32; at c8 and c16 graph capture stops at 576 tokens and
-  `--prefill-schedule-interval` stays at the vLLM default of 1, while c32 extends piecewise
-  graphs to 4096 tokens and sets `--prefill-schedule-interval 64`. DEP4 sets
-  `--prefill-schedule-interval 48` at c128 and keeps the default of 1 at c64.
+  The B200 AgentX lane ([SemiAnalysisAI/InferenceX#3837](https://github.com/SemiAnalysisAI/InferenceX/pull/3837))
+  serves the 0909 launch checkpoint ([deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash](https://huggingface.co/deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash);
+  pick **FP8 (0909)** to match it) with FlashInfer autotuning
+  (`--kernel-config '{"enable_flashinfer_autotune":true}'`), `--gpu-memory-utilization 0.97`
+  and `VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=1` on every point.
+
+  **TP4** serves concurrency 1 to 128 with `--tensor-parallel-size 4`, THP-backed Engram tables
+  (`--engram-config '{"cpu_offload":true,"use_thp":true}'`) and these per-point limits:
+
+  | Concurrency | `--max-num-seqs` | `--max-num-batched-tokens` | `--max-cudagraph-capture-size` |
+  |---|---|---|---|
+  | 1, 4 | 8 | 4096 | 4092 |
+  | 8, 16 | 16, 32 | 8192 | 8190 |
+  | 32, 64, 128 | 64, 128, 256 | 8192 | 8190 |
+
+  Every TP4 point captures piecewise graphs at the DSpark verification multiples
+  `[6,12,18,24,30,36,48,60,72,96,120,144,192,240,288,384,480,576,768,1020,1536,2046,3072,4092]`,
+  extended with `6144,8190` from c8. From c16 it also captures decode-replay graphs separately,
+  with the same `decoder_replay_cudagraph_capture_sizes` as DEP4 below.
+
+  **TP2** at concurrency 1 runs the TP4 c1 settings on two GPUs (`--max-num-seqs 8`,
+  `--max-num-batched-tokens 4096`, capture to 4092).
+
+  **DEP2** (TP1 x DP2 with expert parallelism) serves concurrency 8 to 32 with
+  `--max-num-batched-tokens 4096`. `--max-num-seqs` is per DP rank: 16 at c8 and c16 and 32 at
+  c24 and c32. At c8 and c16 graph capture stops at 576 tokens
+  (`--max-cudagraph-capture-size 576`) and `--prefill-schedule-interval` stays at the vLLM
+  default of 1, while c24 and c32 extend piecewise graphs to 4096 tokens and set
+  `--prefill-schedule-interval 64`.
+
+  **DEP4** (TP1 x DP4) serves concurrency 64 to 128 with `--max-num-batched-tokens 8192` and
+  `--max-cudagraph-capture-size 8190`. `--max-num-seqs` is 64 at c64, 96 at c96 and 128 at
+  c128. It sets `--prefill-schedule-interval 48` at c96 and c128 and keeps the default of 1
+  at c64. Decode-replay graphs are captured separately:
+
+  ```
+  --compilation-config '{"mode":"VLLM_COMPILE","cudagraph_mode":"FULL_AND_PIECEWISE","cudagraph_capture_sizes":[6,12,18,24,30,36,48,60,72,96,120,144,192,240,288,384,480,576,768,1020,1536,2046,3072,4092,6144,8190],"decoder_replay_cudagraph_capture_sizes":[6,12,18,24,30,36,48,60,72,96,120,144,192,240,288,384,480,576,768,1020,1536,2048,2304,2560,2816,3072,3328,3584,3840,4096]}'
+  ```
 
-  For DEP2 at c128, add vLLM's native CPU KV offloading with
+  **DEP2 with host KV** at c64 and c128 adds vLLM's native CPU KV offloading with
   `--kv-offloading-backend native --kv-offloading-size 32` (GiB per DP rank, 64 GiB per
-  server), `--gpu-memory-utilization 0.955` and `--max-num-seqs 48`.
+  server), `--gpu-memory-utilization 0.955` and `--max-num-seqs 48`. `--max-num-seqs` is per
+  DP rank, so the server runs up to 96 sequences: nothing queues at c64, and about 32 clients
+  wait at c128. It keeps `--prefill-schedule-interval` at 1 and captures graphs only up to
+  576 tokens (`--max-cudagraph-capture-size 576`), as DEP2 does at c8 and c16.
+
+  In the command builder, pick **B200** and the **FP8 (0909)** checkpoint, and tick
+  **Speculative decoding** and **Text only** (both are opt-in). **Tensor Parallel** then
+  renders the TP2 c1 settings, and **Data + Expert Parallel** renders the DEP2 c24/c32 engine
+  settings. The builder's DEP spans all eight GPUs, so set `--data-parallel-size 2` (or 4 for
+  DEP4), select the matching GPUs, change the vLLM Router's `--intra-node-data-parallel-size`
+  to the same value, and take the per-concurrency values above.
 
   ### Aggregate serving on B300

commits.message:
[Attention] Use trtllm-gen for the FlashInfer DCP prefill context pass (#62029)

Signed-off-by: Gagandeep Kang <gagandeep.kang@cohere.com>
Signed-off-by: Summer Yang <girasoleyang@gmail.com>
Co-authored-by: Cursor <cursoragent@cursor.com>
Co-authored-by: Summer Yang <girasoleyang@gmail.com>
Co-authored-by: Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

files.patch:
@@ -645,3 +645,119 @@ def test_flashinfer_trtllm_prefill_with_baseline(
         torch.testing.assert_close(output, output_trtllm, atol=atol, rtol=rtol),
         f"{torch.max(torch.abs(output - output_trtllm))}",
     )
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("num_heads", [(8, 1), (16, 2)])
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("dcp_world_size", [2, 8])
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("head_size", [64, 128, 256])
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("block_size", [16, 64])
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("context_lens", [[0, 37, 1000, 0, 4096], [0, 0]])
+@torch.inference_mode
+def test_flashinfer_dcp_prefill_trtllm_context(
+    num_heads: tuple[int, int],
+    dcp_world_size: int,
+    head_size: int,
+    block_size: int,
+    context_lens: list[int],
+) -> None:
+    """The trtllm-gen DCP context pass matches the native one, and gives
+    requests without local context a zero output and a -inf LSE."""
+    from vllm.v1.attention.backends.flashinfer import BatchDCPPrefillWrapper
+
+    set_random_seed(42)
+    device = "cuda"
+    dtype = torch.bfloat16
+    num_blocks = 4096 // block_size * len(context_lens) + 1
+    num_qo_heads, num_kv_heads = num_heads
+    sm_scale = head_size**-0.5
+
+    batch_size = len(context_lens)
+    ctx_lens = torch.tensor(context_lens, dtype=torch.int32)
+    q_lens = torch.randint(1, 64, (batch_size,), dtype=torch.int32)
+    qo_indptr = torch.zeros(batch_size + 1, dtype=torch.int32)
+    torch.cumsum(q_lens, dim=0, out=qo_indptr[1:])
+    num_pages = (ctx_lens + block_size - 1) // block_size
+    kv_indptr = torch.zeros(batch_size + 1, dtype=torch.int32)
+    torch.cumsum(num_pages, dim=0, out=kv_indptr[1:])
+    last_page_lens = ctx_lens - (num_pages - 1).clamp(min=0) * block_size
+
+    max_pages = max(int(num_pages.max()), 1)
+    block_tables = torch.randperm(num_blocks, dtype=torch.int32, device=device)[
+        : batch_size * max_pages
+    ].view(batch_size, max_pages)
+    kv_indices = torch.cat(
+        [block_tables[i, :n] for i, n in enumerate(num_pages.tolist())]
+    )
+
+    # K and V packed in the head dim, as in the FlashInfer backend's KV cache.
+    kv_cache = torch.randn(
+        num_blocks, num_kv_heads, block_size, 2 * head_size, dtype=dtype, device=device
+    )
+    kv_cache_tuple = kv_cache.split(head_size, dim=-1)
+    # The context pass sees the query heads of all DCP ranks.
+    query = torch.randn(
+        int(qo_indptr[-1]),
+        num_qo_heads * dcp_world_size,
+        head_size,
+        dtype=dtype,
+        device=device,
+    )
+    workspace = torch.zeros(128 * 1024 * 1024, dtype=torch.uint8, device=device)
+
+    def run_context(use_trtllm_context):
+        wrapper = BatchDCPPrefillWrapper(
+            "HND", workspace, use_trtllm_context=use_trtllm_context
+        )
+        wrapper.plan(
+            qo_indptr_cpu=qo_indptr,
+            paged_kv_indptr_cpu=kv_indptr,
+            paged_kv_indices=kv_indices,
+            paged_kv_last_page_len_cpu=last_page_lens,
+            kv_lens_cpu=ctx_lens,
+            page_size=block_size,
+            num_qo_heads=num_qo_heads,
+            dcp_world_size=dcp_world_size,
+            num_kv_heads=num_kv_heads,
+            head_dim=head_size,
+            sm_scale=sm_scale,
+            window_left=-1,
+            logits_soft_cap=None,
+            q_data_type=dtype,
+            kv_cache_dtype=dtype,
+            prefill_fixed_split_size=-1,
+            # Split-KV scratch for the native pass would not fit the workspace.
+            disable_split_kv=True,
+            block_tables=block_tables,
+        )
+        assert (wrapper._context is wrapper._trtllm_context) == use_trtllm_context
+        return wrapper._context.run(
+            query, kv_cache_tuple, k_scale=1.0, v_scale=1.0, return_lse=True
+        )
+
+    output, lse = run_context(True)
+    has_context = torch.repeat_interleave(ctx_lens > 0, q_lens).to(device)
+    assert torch.all(output[~has_context] == 0)
+    assert torch.all(lse[~has_context] == float("-inf"))
+    if not has_context.any():
+        return
+
+    ref_output, ref_lse = run_context(False)
+    torch.testing.assert_close(
+        output[has_context], ref_output[has_context], atol=1e-2, rtol=1e-2
+    )
+    torch.testing.assert_close(
+        lse[has_context], ref_lse[has_context], atol=1e-2, rtol=1e-3
+    )
+
+
+def test_trtllm_dcp_context_workspace_fit() -> None:
+    """Batches whose LSE scratch exceeds the trtllm-gen workspace fall back to
+    the native context pass."""
+    from vllm.v1.attention.backends.flashinfer import TrtllmDCPContextWrapper
+
